outcome: Change in pelvic floor muscle strength over time
cohort: 543 parous women, recruited 5-10 years after first delivery
finding: Pelvic muscle strength increased minimally over time (1.2 cm H2O per 5 years on average), but the change was associated with mode of delivery and obesity.
mod_finding: Women who delivered by cesarean only had almost no change in pelvic floor muscle strength over 5 years, while those with vaginal deliveries (with or without forceps) experienced an increase in strength.
